help.title: About Product variants
help.overview: A variant is one sellable SKU of a variable product, defined by its combination of attribute values (for example Red / XL). The cart and the till charge the variant's own price when it has one. Only an active variant can be sold.

sections.title: Identity
items: Product is required and fixed for good: stock rows and order lines are keyed on the product and the variant together.
Attribute combination is the set of attribute-and-value pairs. Two live variants of one product cannot share a combination.
SKU and barcode identify it; a scanned variant barcode adds that exact variant at the till.

sections.title: Price, weight, media
items: Price, compare-at price, and cost work like the product's. A variant without a price sells at the product price.
Weight, dimensions, main image, and display order describe the variant on the storefront picker.

sections.title: Stock
items: A variant of a tracked product is stock-tracked unless track inventory is off on the variant. Then each warehouse needs an inventory row for this variant.
With no row in an active warehouse, checkout refuses the variant as out of stock.

sections.title: Status and the product
items: Active variants are sold; an inactive variant is removed from carts the next time they are priced.
The product's variant list, variant count, and has-variants flag follow its live variants; a product with at least one variant can be published without its own price.
Deleting is a soft delete and it can be restored.
